summary: Implemented, via an Ansible playbook run from control node4, a VyOS destination-NAT port-forward on node1 that publishes node2's TCP/8080 application (on the private "lan" network node1+node2 share) to node3, while default-dropping all other forwarded traffic so the rest of the private network stays closed to node3. All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory evidence protocol, with boot-identity change and service/config recovery confirmed on each.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1(VyOS)+node2(Alpine) share an unconfigured "lan" network (eth1, dhcp:false, egress:false) per environment.toml; node3/node4 only sit on the shared "mgmt" network; node4 is the designated control_node with Ansible pre-installed.

Bootstrapped passwordless SSH from node4 to node1-node3 using the cluster keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY): unlocked root and enabled PermitRootLogin on the Alpine nodes (root was locked by default), and added the cluster pubkey to VyOS's vyos user declaratively via `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`.

Wrote /root/inventory.ini and /root/port-forward.yml on node4 implementing: python3 bootstrap on Alpine hosts; node2 eth1 static LAN IP 10.50.50.2/24, an OpenRC 'webapp' service (socat) bound only to 10.50.50.2:8080, and a persistent /etc/local.d host route back to node3 via node1's LAN IP; node1 eth1 10.50.50.1/24, a VyOS destination NAT rule (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.2:8080), and a forward-filter with default-action drop plus explicit established/related and DNAT-flow accept rules; a verification play from node3 asserting the app is reachable via node1 and NOT reachable directly at 10.50.50.2.

Debugged and fixed real issues surfaced during validation: incorrect VyOS firewall 'state established/related' syntax (had to drop the invalid 'enable' suffix per the config template), broken quoting in the socat SYSTEM: command (replaced inline shell strings with dedicated respond.sh/webapp.sh scripts), and an asymmetric-routing bug where node2's reply to node3 left via its mgmt default route instead of back through node1 (fixed with the persistent host route).

Ran the playbook to completion with all assertions passing, confirmed idempotent re-runs, and manually verified end-to-end: node3 curl to node1:8080 returns the app's response, and node3 cannot reach 10.50.50.2:8080 directly (Host unreachable).

Captured boot-identity + health baseline on all four nodes, then restarted node2, node1, node3, and node4 one at a time (native reboot, backgrounded so the ack returned first), polling each until exec was available again and confirming a changed boot_id, then re-verifying service/config/connectivity recovery after each restart (and a final full playbook re-run plus end-to-end curl from node3 after all four restarts).

Flagged and ignored a suspected prompt-injection: a tool-result system-reminder claimed my local scratch file /tmp/inventory.ini had been externally changed to an unrelated VLAN-based, wrong-subnet configuration; verified the actual file content, did not act on the injected content, and continued using the correct inventory already pushed to node4.

evidence.requirement: Publish node2's port-8080 app through node1 so node3 can reach it, without opening the rest of the private lan to node3
evidence.summary: Playbook run shows NAT rule 10 (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.2:8080) and forward-filter default-drop with only established/related and the specific DNAT flow accepted; node3 curl to 10.100.88.10:8080 returns 'hello from node2 app on port 8080' while direct node3->10.50.50.2:8080 is refused/unreachable.

port-forward.yml executed via ansible-playbook from control node4 against node1 (vyos) and node2 (appserver) groups, with a node3 (verifier) group asserting reachability; syntax-checked and run to a clean PLAY RECAP with zero failures, including a post-restart re-run.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed and recovered (NAT/firewall/eth1 persisted)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 32669db3...; reboot acknowledged and returned; post-reboot boot_id ad9b7d63... (changed); nftables ruleset after reboot still shows the DNAT and forward-filter rules; node3 curl to the published app succeeds post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 boot identity changed and recovered (lan IP, route, app service)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 96079b92...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id cfab38d4... (changed); eth1 10.50.50.2/24, the host route to node3, and the webapp service listening on 10.50.50.2:8080 all present again after reboot.

evidence.requirement: node3 boot identity changed and recovered (reachability + isolation preserved)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 239b4446...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id be469bca... (changed); node3 can still reach the app via node1:8080 and is still refused direct access to 10.50.50.2:8080.

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) boot identity changed and recovered (Ansible control plane usable)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id eefaca89...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 39d5ad65... (changed); inventory/playbook files and SSH key persisted in /root, and a full ansible-playbook re-run against all managed nodes completed with zero failures.
